opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kenneth Burch (employee ID E007) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E007.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Kenneth Burch (E007) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; the Analyst role does not own Payroll, so admin is not permitted. Write is within policy, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Kenneth Burch (E007) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; admin never. Requested write exceeds the maximum for a contractor with basic training, so recommend granting read.
reason: There is conflicting evidence about Kenneth Burch's (E007) employment type. HR states full-time Analyst (max write for Payroll), while Security states contractor with basic security training (max read, since write requires advanced training). Granting read satisfies both interpretations and never exceeds any applicable maximum. The requested write level exceeds the contractor maximum, so I grant the maximum allowed under the more restrictive valid reading: read.
